claim_a.claim_text: Two-stage detectors with region proposal networks achieve state-of-the-art object detection accuracy, while one-stage detectors trade accuracy for speed.
claim_a.evidence_quote: Our Faster R-CNN with VGG-16 ... has a frame rate of 5fps on a GPU, while achieving state-of-the-art object detection accuracy on PASCAL VOC 2007, 2012, and MS COCO datasets.

claim_b.claim_text: A one-stage detector trained with focal loss matches or exceeds two-stage detectors in accuracy, eliminating the historical accuracy-speed tradeoff.
claim_b.evidence_quote: We design and train a simple dense detector we call RetinaNet. Our results show that when trained with the focal loss, RetinaNet ... matches the speed of previous one-stage detectors while surpassing the accuracy of all existing state-of-the-art two-stage detectors.

rationale: Both papers are correct in their context: in 2015 two-stage detectors held the SOTA accuracy crown; in 2017 RetinaNet showed that addressing class imbalance with focal loss closes the gap. The contradiction is an era_shift, not a logical conflict.
